title: Perfect complex with residue-field degree-zero fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, let $K$ be a perfect object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], and let $u:\mathcal O_S\to K$ be a morphism in $D(\mathcal O_S)$. Assume that for every point $s\in S$ the map $\kappa(s)=H^0(\mathcal O_S\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))$ induced by $u$ is an isomorphism and $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))=0$ for all $i<0$. Then $H^0(u):\mathcal O_S\to H^0(K)$ is an isomorphism, and Zariski-locally on $S$ there is a decomposition $K\cong\mathcal O_S\oplus P$ in $D(\mathcal O_S)$, where $P$ is perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$ [lem-pc-tor-amplitude-qcoh-test].

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$. By [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] there is an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ on which $K$ is represented by a bounded complex of finite free modules whose term in degree $i$ has rank $d_i=\dim_{\kappa(s)}H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s))$; by hypothesis $d_i=0$ for $i<0$. A bounded complex of flat modules sitting in degrees $\ge0$ computes $K|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal G$ termwise, so it has no cohomology in negative degrees for every $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal G$. As cohomology sheaves are local, $K$ has Tor-amplitude in $[0,\infty)$ on $S$; in particular $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<0$.

source.place: Tag 0E62, proof of lemma-proper-flat-h0, sentence 'This first implies that E has tor amplitude in [0, infinity)'

proof.text: Since $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<0$ we have $\tau_{\le0}K=H^0(K)[0]$, and $u$ factors as $\mathcal O_S\xrightarrow{H^0(u)}H^0(K)\to K$. By naturality, for $s\in S$ the fibre map $\kappa(s)\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s))$ is the composite $\mathcal O_S\otimes\kappa(s)\to H^0(K)\otimes\kappa(s)\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s))$; as it is an isomorphism, the second map is surjective. Applying [lem-sc-perfect-cut-complex-degree-zero] (its Tor-amplitude hypothesis is step 1) gives an open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ and $K|_U\cong H^0(K)|_U\oplus P$ with $P$ perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$.

source.place: Tag 0E62, proof of lemma-proper-flat-h0, application of More on Algebra, Lemma better-cut-complex-in-two

proof.text: On $U$ as in step 2, $M=H^0(K)|_U$ is a direct summand of $K|_U$, hence perfect by [lem-pc-perfect-summand], and of Tor-amplitude in $[0,\infty)$ by step 1; since $H^i(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal G)=\mathcal Tor_{-i}(M,\mathcal G)$ vanishes for $i<0$, $M$ is flat. On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U$, [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] represents $M|_V$ by a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules with cohomology only in degree $0$; exactness in degrees $\ge1$ splits $P^{\ge0}$ from the top, so $Z^0=\ker(P^0\to P^1)$ is a direct summand of $P^0$, and $M(V)=\operatorname{coker}(P^{-1}\to Z^0)$ is finitely presented. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] it is finite projective, so $H^0(K)$ is finite locally free on $S$.

source.place: Tag 0E62, proof of lemma-proper-flat-h0, paragraph 'Since E has tor amplitude in [0, infinity) ... finite locally free'

proof.text: On $U$ as in step 2, $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s)\cong(H^0(K)\otimes\kappa(s))\oplus(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s))$ because $H^0(K)$ is flat (step 3), and $P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s)$ has no cohomology in degrees $\le0$; so $H^0(K)\otimes\kappa(s)\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s))$ is an isomorphism, and by the factorization of step 2 so is $H^0(u)\otimes\kappa(s):\kappa(s)\to H^0(K)\otimes\kappa(s)$, for every $s\in S$. Both $\mathcal O_S$ and $H^0(K)$ are finite locally free (step 3), so [lem-sc-finite-locally-free-residue-isomorphism] shows that $H^0(u)$ is an isomorphism. Substituting it into the splitting of step 2 gives $K|_U\cong\mathcal O_U\oplus P$ with $P$ perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$.
